name: cold-start-overdue-drift
definition: Splits the existing `overdue` signal (practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py, is_overdue) into two distinct kinds: cold_start_overdue (a future whose window.to already lay in the past on the very night it was first notarized — announced_at[:10] == first seen date and is_overdue true at NOTARIZED time) versus drift_overdue (a future that was NOT overdue when the observatory first saw it, and only became overdue on a later run while still OPEN, meaning it outlived the window it was announced with). Tonight's run.json shows 100/100 notarized futures already listed as overdue on their first night (foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-08/run.json: `notarized` and `overdue` are the same 100 ids) — entirely cold_start_overdue, since this is the observatory's first night and every future is by definition being seen for the first time. drift_overdue cannot exist yet and will only become measurable from the second run onward.
test_rule: On each nightly run, for every OPEN future newly flagged overdue, check whether it was already overdue in the immediately preceding run's overdue list (or is cold-start, i.e. this run is its NOTARIZED run). If it was open, not overdue, and NOT in a prior run's overdue list, tag it drift_overdue in that night's run summary. The sensor is worth promoting once at least one drift_overdue case has actually been observed and its window/severity history inspected by hand.
falsification: If, once a second night exists, every single overdue future turns out to be cold_start_overdue for many consecutive nights (i.e. GDACS simply never keeps an episode open past its own stated window), the drift_overdue class would be empty by construction and this sensor would add a label that never fires — worth dropping rather than promoting.

implementation.how: overdue_kind() decides the split from committed records alone: a future is cold_start_overdue when the window end it was announced with already lay in the past at its own announced_at, and drift_overdue otherwise. The window end as of notarization is read back through the revision history, which is append-only, so a later window extension cannot relabel a cold start. Nightly runs record both lists in run.json from the next run on.
implementation.not_promoted_because: The proposal asks for promotion only after at least one drift_overdue case has been observed and its history inspected by hand. Tonight there are none and there cannot be: every future in the registry was notarized on the observatory's first night, so all 100 overdue flags are cold starts by construction. Building the split now and promoting it later keeps the two decisions apart — the code exists so the evidence can appear, and the evidence still has to appear.
implementation.watch_for: the first entry in run.json's overdue_drift list

promotion.settles: the proposal's own bar for promotion, named in test_rule above: at least one drift_overdue case observed and its window/severity history inspected by hand.
promotion.case: gdacs-fl-1104081 (GDACS flood, China): NOTARIZED 2026-08-12T22:14:16+00:00 with window.to = 2026-08-13T01:00:00, inside its window at notarization (not cold_start_overdue); no REVISED event in its history; first appeared in overdue_drift on 2026-08-13's run and again on 2026-08-14's, two consecutive nights, still OPEN.
promotion.test_rule_held: the falsification clause's opposite outcome -- 'every single overdue future turns out to be cold_start_overdue for many consecutive nights ... the drift_overdue class would be empty by construction' -- did not happen; a real, inspectable case exists and persists.
promotion.kept_unchanged: definition, test_rule and falsification are the machine's original text (2026-08-08) and match the running code (overdue_kind, futures.py) as written; no threshold changed.

review.outcome: stays PROMOTED; the cold_start/drift split itself is unaffected, but the is_overdue check it is built on was wrong for every NWS future it has ever classified -- repaired the same night
review.why: obs-2026-08-26-1.json found that is_overdue (this sensor's own implementation, futures.py) compared window.to against now_iso by truncating both to their first 19 characters, which drops NWS's real UTC offset while leaving GDACS's already-naive-UTC values unaffected. Every one of the 13 NWS futures this observatory has flagged overdue since NWS was audited in (2026-08-22 through tonight) recomputes as not overdue once both timestamps are converted to real UTC instants -- a 100% false-positive rate for one source, invisible against GDACS because GDACS's window fields never carried an offset to test the bug against. This proposal's own definition and falsification clause were written and reviewed entirely against GDACS data; adding a second, differently-formatted source silently invalidated an assumption neither the proposal nor the promotion review had reason to name.
review.watch_for: any other function that reads a raw source timestamp and could carry the same naive-comparison assumption the next time a source with a different timestamp convention is added -- named but not fully audited in obs-2026-08-26-1.json's left_alone.
